title: Virtual Care Rule on Patient Location, Established Status, Age and In-Person Contact
content:
A Virtual Care clinician may treat only a patient physically located, at the moment of the encounter, in a state the visit type's licensed states cover. The clauses below state that rule and the other conditions on who may be seen in a Virtual Care encounter.

## Clauses

**1. Physical location.** A clinician may treat only a patient physically located in a state the visit type's licensed states cover at the moment of the encounter.

**2. Attestation at the start.** The patient attests being physically in a covered state when the encounter starts. The basis is the patient's own statement, given for this encounter at the moment it starts, before the encounter proceeds. Where the visit type's location attestation setting is Yes, the attestation is recorded at the start of every encounter. The start of an encounter is the moment a clinician opens it and the patient attests their location.

**3. Patient elsewhere.** A patient elsewhere is told to use local care; the request is cancelled as clinic-initiated.

**4. Established patients.** Where the visit type does not accept new patients, the patient must have a completed visit in the group within the last established-patient lookback months of the visit type.

**5. Age.** Patients younger than the visit type's minimum age are not served, and a parent or guardian joins for patients younger than the visit type's guardian age.

**6. In-person contact.** Where the visit type's in-person interval is above 0, continued virtual care requires a completed in-person visit in the department within that many calendar months before the encounter; otherwise the patient is booked in person first. The in-person visit read is the latest scheduled date among the patient's In-Person Appointments with status completed in the encounter's department, across all history up to the handling date.

**7. Safety readiness.** Where the visit type's emergency contact setting or its safety plan setting is Yes, the emergency contact and safety plan are confirmed at the start.

**8. Device.** The device the visit type requires must be available to the patient.

## What each clause reads

| Clause | What it is decided on |
|---|---|
| Physical location | The patient's own attestation of the state they are physically in, given for this encounter at its start |
| Established patients | A completed visit in the group within the lookback |
| In-person contact | The latest completed In-Person Appointment in the encounter's department |
| Age | The patient's age against the visit type's minimum age and guardian age |

## Cases (hypothetical patients and visit-type figures)

**Location.** A visit type whose licensed states cover Ohio only; at the start the patient attests being physically in Indiana. Indiana is not covered, so the clinician may not treat the patient: the patient is told to use local care and the request is cancelled as clinic-initiated. Had the patient attested being in Ohio, clause 1 would be met.

**In-person contact.** A visit type with an in-person interval of 12 calendar months. The patient's latest completed In-Person Appointment in the encounter's department took place 5 months before the encounter: the requirement is met. Had it taken place 20 months before, the requirement would not be met and the patient is booked in person first. A completed In-Person Appointment in a different department is not an in-person visit in the encounter's department and does not meet this clause.

**Interval of 0.** A visit type whose in-person interval is 0 carries no in-person contact requirement under clause 6.

**Age.** A visit type with a minimum age of 12 and a guardian age of 16: an 11-year-old is not served; a 14-year-old meets the minimum age and a parent or guardian joins.
